quote: “A classic is a book that has never finished saying what it has to say.”
source: Italo Calvino, Why Read the Classics?, definition 6 (trans. Patrick Creagh, 1986)

evidence.where: The New York Review of Books, 9 October 1986, printing the essay in Patrick Creagh’s translation; definition 6 read verbatim there in the January verdict 01-cfl-09, which this ruling rechecks against the same record
evidence.edition: The Uses of Literature, trans. Patrick Creagh, Harcourt Brace Jovanovich, 1986
evidence.locator: Why Read the Classics?, definition 6 of the essay’s fourteen

reason: Definition 6 in Creagh’s 1986 translation, verbatim. Verified in January but it did not land; Calvino shipped once (If on a winter’s night a traveler), so this would be two of three, and shipped.js finds the line unshipped.
